details: A 33 g CO2 charge expands to fill roughly a 150 N bladder at surface pressure; gas laws set the sizing.
Inflation must complete in seconds; orifice and bladder volume are matched so pressure peaks fast but safe.
Buoyancy appears only after inflation, so the pre-inflation state must still keep the wearer afloat briefly.
Hydrostatic inflators trigger near 10 cm of water pressure, avoiding rain-triggered false inflation.
